records.text: Anonymous aviation sources told Owens that a private flight was supposed to land at Million Air in Page, Arizona, but changed at the last second to Signature, and that the flight appeared unusual.
records.speaker: Flight and airport sources (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: Multiple people have confirmed that this plane was a little bit weird that day. It was supposed to land in Page, Arizona, in Million Air FBO. Last second, it made a change. As you guys know, an FBO was just a private terminal. So if you're in a public airport, you go to terminal seven. If you're flying private, you go to FBO, and it has a name. So that plane was supposed to land into an FBO called Million Air. Last second—I mean, and I mean last second—that plane decided to change and say, "We are going to instead land into Signature," a different FBO. Apparently it landed into Signature. That's what we were—that's certainly what we were told.

verification.notes: The claim rests on unnamed pilots and airport contacts. Live searches found no accessible flight plan, FBO handling record, ATC record, or statement from Million Air or Signature confirming a last-second terminal change. The alleged unusualness of the flight is also subjective and cannot be resolved without those records.
